meta.title: Terms of Service
meta.description: The terms for using WattPrint, a household electricity tracker and bill forecast.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms (“Terms”) apply when you use WattPrint: the landing page and the dashboard. By creating an account or continuing to use the service, you agree to these Terms.

service.title: 1. What WattPrint is
service.body: WattPrint shows your home's electricity use, estimates how much each appliance uses, forecasts your electricity bill and suggests ways to save. Every figure is for information: per-appliance numbers are estimates made from the main meter, not separate measurements, and a forecast bill can differ from your utility's bill. The real bill is always the one your electricity company sends.

accounts.title: 2. Accounts and security
accounts.body: When you create an account, you agree to:

items.confidential: Keep your sign-in details to yourself.
items.notify: Tell us soon if you suspect someone else got into your account.
items.responsible: Be responsible for everything done under your account.

acceptableUse.title: 3. Using it properly
acceptableUse.body: You agree not to misuse the service or help others to. In particular, you will not:

items.laws: Break Vietnamese law, including the rules on cybersecurity and personal data protection.
items.security: Try to get past sign-in, rate limits or other safeguards without clear permission.
items.abuse: Run denial-of-service attacks, guess passwords automatically or reach other people's data.

home.title: 4. Your home and its members
home.body: Each account belongs to one home. The owner is the person who set the home up and can invite others as members, who see either everything or daily figures only; a sample-home viewer can only read. The sample homes on the sign-in page are public recordings from research datasets (REFIT, Plegma, ENERTALK) replayed for you to try, not homes of WattPrint users. Trial guest accounts are deleted after 24 hours, when the next trial guest arrives.

assistant.title: 5. The Wappi assistant
assistant.body: Wappi is an automated system, not a person. Figures in its answers come from your home's data, but its explanations can be wrong or incomplete, so do not treat them as professional advice. Do not type or speak sensitive details to Wappi: in a written question, phone numbers, ID numbers, emails, card and account numbers are replaced by a label before it is stored and sent, but this only spots familiar formats, not names or addresses. Voice recordings are sent as they are.

liability.title: 6. Limit of liability
liability.body: The service is provided “as is”, with no warranty of any kind, express or implied, as far as the law allows. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss from using or not being able to use the service, including decisions about electricity or money made from estimated or forecast figures.

termination.title: 7. Ending and deleting your account
termination.body: You can end these Terms at any time by deleting your account from the account menu in the dashboard (see the Privacy Policy for what is erased). We may suspend or end accounts that break these Terms.

law.title: 8. Governing law and contact
law.body: These Terms are governed by Vietnamese law. For any question, contact ntgiang141105@gmail.com.

meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: How WattPrint collects, uses, shares and deletes your data.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page says what data WattPrint collects, who receives it, how long it is kept and how you delete it. It is written with Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 91/2025/QH15) and Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP in mind.

controller.title: 1. Who is responsible for your data
controller.body: Your data is managed, and answered for, by an individual:
controller.name: Nguyễn Trường Giang

collected.title: 2. Data we collect
collected.body: Only what the service needs to run:

items.account: Account: email and name (typed at sign-up, or taken from your Google account if you sign in with Google). Keycloak keeps the password as a hash; we cannot read it.
items.session: Sign-in session: an access token in a cookie, and the IP address that the server and Keycloak log to stop abuse.
items.home: Your home: its name, province or city, number of people, floor area, home type, billing cycle day, its members and what they may see, and the notification choices you set.
items.energy: Electricity: your home's meter readings (about every 10 seconds), totals, per-appliance estimates and on/off times, expected use, forecast bills, alerts and savings plans. This data can reveal your household's daily routine.
items.assistant: Chats with Wappi: questions and answers are stored with your account, along with the figures and queries used to answer. In questions, phone numbers, ID numbers, emails, card and account numbers are replaced by a label before they are stored and sent on; names and addresses are not detected.
items.voice: Voice: when you speak to Wappi, the recording is sent as it is (it cannot be masked) to be turned into text; when you listen to an answer, the spoken audio is kept for 30 days so it need not be made again.
items.guest: Trial guests: a temporary account with no real email, deleted after 24 hours (expired ones are cleared when a new guest arrives).

sharing.title: 3. Who receives your data
sharing.body: Some parts of the service are handled by others, some of them outside Vietnam. WattPrint logs what its own server sends (receiver, purpose, kind of data, level of detail, never the content); the entries about you from the last 30 days are shown in Settings > Privacy:

items.ai: OpenRouter (outside Vietnam), and AstralX when OpenRouter fails (Wappi's AI models, including question screening, document search and result ranking): your question, the open conversation and what Wappi looks up from your home's data, such as daily or hourly electricity figures, appliance names, bills, alerts and some details about the home. By default Wappi sees daily figures only (sample homes: hourly); the owner can allow hourly, and then night-by-night standby results may be sent too. WattPrint asks OpenRouter to use only providers that keep no data and do not train on it; this request is not applied to AstralX. We have not confirmed where AstralX's servers are, how long it keeps data or whether it passes it on.
items.voice: AstralX (voice): your recording as it is, to turn into text, and the text of an answer to be read aloud.
items.weather: OpenWeather (weather): only the province or city coordinates of your home, never your address or name.
items.google: Google (sign-in, if you choose it): Google knows that you sign in to WattPrint its way. Telegram (feedback): when you press 👎, the rating and the answer's ID go to the maintainer. Only if you tick the box to include the content are the question and answer (which may hold your home's figures) sent too, and the maintainer can read them. Email servers: your email address, with alerts, weekly summaries, and account verification or reset mail. Account mail sent by Keycloak and Google sign-in are not in the log.

sharing.abroad: Each of them has its own policy on the data it gets. Data already sent to them cannot be deleted from WattPrint. We do not use your data for advertising and we have built no advertising trackers into the service.

bases.title: 4. Why we may handle your data
bases.body: Each use rests on a clear ground:

contract.title: To provide the service
contract.body: Creating your account, signing you in, showing electricity and bills, running Wappi.

consent.title: You agree
consent.body: You sign up yourself, turn email notifications on yourself and choose to talk to Wappi. Settings > Privacy has consent switches for Wappi, voice and email, and each change is recorded. Until you consent, or after you withdraw, the server refuses: Wappi and voice send nothing out, and alert and weekly summary emails are not sent.

interests.title: Protecting the service
interests.body: Rate limits, blocking attacks and spotting unusual access.

statutory.title: What the law requires
statutory.body: Giving information when a competent authority makes a valid request.

cookies.title: 5. Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: We use no advertising or behaviour-tracking cookies. Only what the service needs to run:

items.session: Three sign-in cookies (.access, .refresh, .id), set HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, plus Secure in production. While you sign in there is also a short-lived cookie (10 minutes) that confirms the sign-in, and Keycloak sets its own session cookies on its own domain.
items.theme: Your light, dark or system choice is kept in your own browser.

retention.title: 6. How long we keep it
retention.body: The more detailed the data, the shorter it is kept. The owner can erase the electricity history at any time (section 8).

items.readings: Meter readings (about every 10 seconds) and per-appliance estimates: 30 days. Per-minute totals and appliance on/off runs: 90 days. Older ones are deleted automatically.
items.rollups: Hourly totals: 400 days. Daily totals: 800 days. Hourly expected use: 400 days. Alerts: 400 days. Forecasts: not yet deleted automatically, kept until erased (section 8). Bills: the last 25 cycles.
items.account: Profile, plans and chats (with their figures and queries): kept until you delete them. Detailed records of each of Wappi's lookups: 30 days. The system's meter-processing logs: 90 days (the latest successful run of each home is kept). Spoken audio: 30 days. Ended watches: 90 days. Outbound log: 90 days.
items.guest: Trial guest accounts: 24 hours, cleared when a new guest arrives.

rights.title: 7. Your rights
rights.body: Under Law No. 91/2025/QH15 and Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP you have these rights over your data. Send a request to the email in section 1; we answer within the time the law sets.

items.access: To know and see your data. Settings > Privacy shows what is kept, since when, and what was sent outside.
items.correct: To correct wrong data. You can edit your home and notification choices in settings; for your name or email, write to the email in section 1.
items.withdraw: To withdraw consent with the switches in Settings > Privacy, or by turning email notifications off in Settings.
items.erase: To delete your data: do it yourself in the app, see section 8.
items.complain: To complain, report or sue if you think your data was handled unlawfully.

deletion.title: 8. Deleting data and your account
deletion.body: In Settings > Privacy: the owner can erase the electricity history before a day or all of it (not for sample homes; chats are not erased with it and may still hold old figures); each person can delete all their own chats in the home, with the audio. To delete your account, choose Delete account on that page or in the account menu. Your profile, chats, savings plans, the watches you set, your choices and your sign-in account are deleted (if deleting the sign-in account fails, you are asked to try again). If you are the only person in your home, the home goes too, with its readings, totals and alerts; the meter is unlinked from it, not deleted. Deletion covers the running system, not what was already sent to others.
deletion.limit: An owner with other members cannot delete the account yet: the members must first leave or be removed by the owner. The server supports inviting, changing what a member sees, removing and leaving, but the app has no screens for these yet; send the request to the email in section 1.

ai.title: 9. The Wappi assistant and automated processing
ai.body: About the use of AI in WattPrint:

items.automated: Wappi is an automated system. It is not a person, and nobody reads each answer before you see it.
items.estimates: Per-appliance figures are estimates. They are worked out from the main meter by an appliance-recognition model, not from separate meters, and are labelled “estimated”.
items.providers: Your question and figures go to the model providers (section 3) so Wappi can answer. We cannot control what they do with them afterwards; weigh that before you ask.
items.training: Appliance-recognition models are trained on public datasets (REFIT, Plegma, ENERTALK). The expected-use model, however, is trained on your own home's data. Who can see your home's data: the owner, and members at the level granted (a “daily only” member sees nothing finer than a day). Operators with access to the server and database can still read it.
